values: Edit Book loads an existing document and allows the user to update metadata or replace its PDF source using Local Upload or Fetch from URL. Metadata-only changes preserve reading progress and offline data. Replacing the source requires confirmation, invalidates source-dependent reading data and must be completed transactionally. The screen also provides a clearly separated permanent Delete Document action.
SCR-07 Edit Book design showing prefilled metadata, source replacement controls, file properties and Danger Zone.
Overview of loading, metadata/source changes, save, cancel and permanent deletion.
Display a Back to Library action above the page title.
If unsaved changes exist, use the same discard confirmation as Cancel.
The screen operates on the Book ID supplied by the origin screen.
Select Local Upload as the active source method.
Its initial state reflects the existing sourceType.
Allow selection of a replacement PDF and display its file name.
Enabled only when Local Upload is selected.
Display properties of the currently stored or newly selected local PDF.
Recommended fields: file name, pages, size and uploaded date; hide for REMOTE_URL when not applicable.
Select Remote URL as the active source method.
Selecting it disables Browse and enables URL input.
Display and allow editing of the PDF source URL.
Enabled only when Fetch from URL is selected.
Required text input prefilled with the current title.
Required text input prefilled with the current author.
Optional text input supporting Common Era and BCE years.
Database type NVARCHAR(10); examples: 2021, 180 BC and 300 BCE.
Display existing tags as removable chips and allow new tags.
Optional multi-line summary prefilled with the current value.
Validate and persist modified source and/or metadata.
Disable when nothing changed or while saving.
Discard unsaved changes and return to the origin screen.
Require confirmation when the form is dirty.
Explain the permanent effects of Delete Document.
Keep visually separated from Save/Cancel actions.
Display main navigation and highlight Library.
Only one navigation item is active.
Display application version and Online/Offline mode.
Remote URL validation and source replacement require Online mode.
Retrieve the selected Book and prefill source, metadata, tags and summary.
Show loading until required data is available.
If the Book does not exist or loading fails, show Retry and Back actions.
Do not display stale data from another Book.
Select Local Upload, enable Browse, display current file name/properties and disable URL input.
The current stored PDF remains unchanged until Save succeeds.
Select Fetch from URL, enable and prefill URL input, and disable Browse.
Hide local file properties unless a retained local copy must be shown separately.
Validate the newly selected PDF and show its name and properties as pending data.
Accept one PDF within the configured size limit.
Reject unsupported, empty, corrupted or oversized files and retain the existing source.
The stored PDF is never replaced before successful Save.
Enable controls for the selected radio and disable the other method.
Retained disabled values are not validated or submitted.
Validate HTTP/HTTPS syntax, accessibility and PDF content for a changed URL.
Handle redirect, timeout, HTTP errors and content-type mismatch; backend validation may be required.
Prevent changing to or validating a new Remote URL while offline.
Existing metadata may still be edited when permitted.
Trim and normalize optional publishYear; accept YYYY, YYYY BC and YYYY BCE up to 10 characters.
Examples: 180bc → 180 BC. Reject unsupported text and values longer than NVARCHAR(10).
Allow adding and removing tag chips without submitting the form on Enter.
Mark the form dirty when source or metadata differs from the loaded Book.
Disable Save Changes when no effective change exists.
Validate Title, Author, Publish Year and only the currently selected source.
Show inline errors and focus the first invalid control.
Update metadata and updatedAt without changing reading progress, favorite state or offline copy.
No PDF storage operation is required.
Treat changed sourceType, local PDF or remote URL as a source replacement.
A URL changed to another URL is also a source replacement.
Before saving a replacement source, warn that page count, progress and offline data may be reset.
Canceling the confirmation returns to the edit form.
For LOCAL_UPLOAD replacement, upload the new PDF to temporary/application storage before updating the Book.
Do not remove the old application copy until the database update succeeds.
For REMOTE_URL replacement, store the validated URL and sourceType = REMOTE_URL.
Do not automatically save the new PDF to IndexedDB.
After successful source replacement, set lastReadPage = 0, readingStatus = UNREAD, clear lastReadAt and recalculate totalPages.
Favorite and metadata remain unchanged unless explicitly edited.
Remove the old IndexedDB copy from the current browser after source replacement.
Other devices cannot be cleaned automatically; offline copies must be versioned or detected as stale.
After the Book update succeeds, remove the obsolete application-managed source, show success and return/refresh.
Recommended destination: refreshed MD-01 or Library.
On failure, keep the old Book/source valid, remove incomplete new storage and retain form values for Retry.
Do not leave the record pointing to a missing file.
Detect if the Book was changed after the edit form loaded.
Use updatedAt/version for optimistic locking and ask the user to reload.
When Cancel or Back is used with a dirty form, confirm discarding changes.
Declining returns to the form unchanged.
When Delete Document is selected, display a confirmation describing all affected application data.
Delete Book metadata, the application-managed PDF and the current browser's IndexedDB copy, then return to Library.
Do not delete the user's original device file or any remote Internet source.
If deletion fails, keep the user on SCR-07 and display an actionable error.
Avoid partial deletion where possible; reconcile storage if it occurs.
Stack source, metadata and Danger Zone sections and keep actions accessible.
Use a standard file picker on mobile.
Associate labels/errors with inputs and expose radio, disabled and destructive-action states.
Do not communicate validation or danger only by color.
